reasons: The cited clause (Section 7.7) requires Customer to pay 'liquidated damages' of 15% of annual Fees per week of late payment — a Customer-payable liquidated amount triggered by a minor administrative breach that quickly exceeds the contract value, squarely within the rule's walk-away band and failing the fallback (which allows only a capped early-termination fee). Deviation status is correct.

The redline implements the preferred position by deleting the Customer-payable liquidated damages and expressly stating no penalty or similar charge applies, substituting ordinary simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts — an actionable, directionally correct edit that does not create a new Customer liability.

The failed 'minimal edit' check is explained by the fact that the rule requires replacing the entire LD sentence; a bare deletion would leave no late-payment mechanic, so a substitution of standard interest is a proportionate rewrite rather than scope creep. The added cross-reference preserving the Section 7.3 withholding right is a minor, party-favourable clarification.
The comment is accurate, concise, correctly attributes the 15%/week figure, cites the playbook position, and explains the substitution without lecturing.
